annotations.title: Check the whole app before deploying

description: Check how the app uses the chart library, before every deploy and after check_chart: reads the app's own source (never the files generate_chart and setup_fabric_app wrote) and reports, each with file, line and the library call to use instead: hand-written selection glue (a toggle, a second-click guard, a remount to clear) where useBicFilter + selects does it; each chart's filter wiring - the page filter its clicks set and the filters its query or component follows (filtered query, highlight only or none) - with a chart filtered by the filter it sets, several charts sharing one click filter, a chart no page filter reaches, and a panel whose filtered query it isn't given; a "vs" measure in the app's .dax queries that is never blank (BLANK() - 1 is -1); a write that stores a placeholder name ("unknown") when no one is signed in or a time from the browser's clock, a Rayfin entity that takes any name on create or lets any row be updated again (rayfin/data), and a dialog that doesn't hold the keyboard; a card's static text that states an order the reader can change ("highest first"); row positions read from the DOM; the payload's __rowIdx__ / __geo* columns built by hand; a slider beside a chart that draws its own controls (useBicControls); notes kept but never shown on the marks (annotations); a chart outside a BicChartPanel, a fixed height below the panel's minimum, a flex-1 container without min-h-0 / min-w-0; two charts setting the same element id; an installed @bicharts/chart-host older than the generated components need (0.6.86); and @bicharts / Rayfin / Fabric visuals packages behind npm's latest. It also draws every chart under src/charts the way check_chart does and reports any that throw, come out blank or don't pass a click to onSelect. Local and free; npm is only asked for versions, and a stack finding is skipped when npm can't be reached. Layout findings are WARNINGS: a static read can't prove a layout. Fix the app's own files; regenerate a chart rather than edit its generated code.

check_npm.description: Compare the stack with npm's latest (default true).

draw_charts.description: Also draw every chart under src/charts (default true).

project_dir.description: The app's folder. Defaults to the folder setup_fabric_app used, else the working directory or the one project folder inside it.
